A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, and their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. The material in v1 Appendix E is retained under v3 Appendices D.3–D.8.

before.justification: v1 reports original intervention experiments across four agent frameworks, alongside error analyses, attribution analyses, and supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds experiments using Claude-Sonnet-4.6, Gemini-3-Pro, and GPT-5.2.

M1.justification: The frozen-backbone agent procedures, memory mechanisms, raw-experience interventions, and condensed-experience interventions are unchanged. The additional backbones are evaluation configurations, without a revised method or algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine principal benchmarks and the supplementary 2WikiMultiHopQA and Musique tasks. The added backbone experiments reuse existing tasks and environments without introducing distinct task requirements or populations.

E2.justification: ExpeL, Dynamic Cheatsheet, ReasoningBank, and G-Memory remain the studied frameworks, and existing comparisons retain their comparator membership. The newly evaluated language models serve as backbones rather than additional comparison algorithms.

E3.justification: v3 adds Claude-Sonnet-4.6 with ExpeL, Gemini-3-Pro with ReasoningBank, and GPT-5.2 with G-Memory under existing evaluation designs. Previously specified datasets, sample sizes, metrics, and interaction budgets remain unchanged. The abstract reports 13 backbones, although Section 3.1 retains the outdated count of 10.

E4.justification: Appendices D.3–D.5 extend intervention-based robustness checks to three newer backbones, testing persistence of the findings in joint-memory, condensed-only, and multi-agent settings. Existing scaling, failure-case, attribution, and task-dependence analyses are retained without new intervention types.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the reported success rates. The added plots retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 9, 12, and 14 add results for the three new backbones; existing numerical results are retained. For example, GPT-5.2 G-Memory on ALFWorld reports 75.4% unperturbed, 47.0% with execution-trajectory shuffling, and 82.1% with condensed-experience corruption. These extend existing experiments under new model configurations, rather than establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The experience definitions, agent-policy formulation, attribution equations in Section 5.2, and appendix description of the gradient approximation are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the systematic faithfulness investigation, raw-versus-condensed asymmetry, persistence across agent settings and scales, and three proposed explanations. Updating the backbone count from 10 to 13 expands supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly argues that larger backbones should generate better summaries, making poor summary quality an insufficient explanation of unfaithfulness. Added appendix discussion interprets the newer-model results as further generalization evidence. However, D.3 overstates Claude/HotpotQA raw-intervention fluctuations: Figure 9 shows 56–58 against baseline 53, versus 47–56 for condensed interventions.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link to the abstract, providing access information absent from v1. Appendix C's implementation details, decoding settings, retrieval configurations, and interaction budgets remain unchanged. Repository availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to the Gemini 3 Pro model card, the GPT-5 system card, and Zhao et al. (2026) on experience utilization. These are limited citation additions; the related-work organization and principal novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Selected experimental and interpretation paragraphs are expanded, acknowledgements are added, and the template running header is corrected. Appendix E's subsections become D.3–D.8, with corresponding references updated. Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds three result plots, Figures 9, 12, and 14, using the established plotting style. Existing result plots and tables are retained, with appendix renumbering and layout reflow. Figure 1 also corrects 'Tasl Goal' to 'Task Goal'.

improvement.justification: The newer-backbone replications broaden evidence for the existing conclusions, and the code-access information modestly improves reproducibility documentation. These gains are limited by unchanged uncertainty reporting and some overstatement of the added results, particularly the Claude/HotpotQA interpretation in Appendix D.3. Overall, the additions provide a useful incremental improvement.
